a: OSI layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.
TCP is reliable and ordered; UDP is faster but unreliable and unordered.
TCP handshake: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK establishes a connection.
An IP packet has a header (addresses, TTL, etc.) and a payload.
Ports identify applications on a host (e.g. 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS, 22 SSH).
NAT translates private IPs to public IPs so many devices share one public address.
DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses and network config to devices.
ARP maps IP addresses to MAC addresses on a local network.
ICMP carries network diagnostics (e.g. ping echo request/reply).
TLS handshake negotiates keys and certificates before encrypted application data.
HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over one connection for better performance.
HTTP/3 runs over QUIC (UDP) for faster connection setup and better loss recovery.
DNS resolution queries resolvers and name servers to translate a domain to an IP.
A subnet is a logical subdivision of an IP network defined by a mask/CIDR.
CIDR notation like 192.168.1.0/24 specifies network prefix length.
A proxy forwards client requests and can cache, filter, or anonymize traffic.
